title: Utah Mammoth Swing Big, Trade For Mackenzie Weegar - NewsBreak
text:
By Christopher Bagdonas ,
4 hours ago (GIF Courtesy Of GIPHY // Utah Mammoth) Utah Mammoth Swing Big, Trade For Mackenzie Weegar Right now, Utah Mammoth fans should be very happy with how their second year of existence is going. Squarely in the playoff race out west and now a big player at the trade deadline. With injuries and inconsistency plaguing their blue line they have ponied up big time for an answer. Rumors have it they struck a deal with the Flames for Mackenzie Weegar. The former secondary piece of the Matthew Tkachuk trade is playing meaningful hockey once again. He has waived his no-trade clause and will move to Utah. Check out the full details below:
Weegar is signed through 2031 with a $6.25 million cap hit. Even at age 32 he is a good minute muncher that can move the puck. Most importantly, however, is that he’s a right handed defenseman. There’s obviously a premium there, which is why Bill Armstrong parted with a high volume of picks and salary filler in Maatta. Those of you who enjoy analytics can see JFresh’s report on him below:
On a Flames team that is going nowhere fast Weegar has posted 18 assists and 21 points in 60 games. The minus 35 on +/- is not flattering but remember, this Calgary squad is beyond waving the white flag. They already sold on Rasmus Andersson weeks ago. Nazem Kadri is one of the most in-demand names ahead of Friday’s deadline. At the time of writing they are 14th in the Western Conference and 12 points out of a playoff spot. You get the rest…
Initially, this is a pretty fair deal for both sides. Weegar will decline as his deal continues so top-shelf assets like Tij Iginla were never really on the table, right? Sorry Flames fans.
However, he’s still a good player, and fills a big need on the Utah blue line. Him and Mikhail Sergachev on the top pair is very strong. They are sitting on the top wild card spot in the West so it would be silly to not add, especially with the assets and cap space they have stockpiled from their Arizona days.
More Flaming Out? Per PuckPedia, the Flames will now have eight picks across the first three rounds of the 2026 Draft. Friedman touched on prospect Jonathan Castagna. He is a centerman from Cornell picked in the third round of the 2023 Draft. Credit to Craig Conroy for finally deciding to tear things down the right way and get a big time collection of picks together.
Once again, the aforementioned Kadri is definitely one of the top names on trade boards. Blake Coleman is another veteran piece signed until 2027 that contenders are sniffing around. However, could younger pieces like Morgan Frost or Matt Coronato get sent out? At this point just about anything is on the table for the Flames.
Shocker… Crusty Sock Jeff Marek Gets Played By An Agent Again After lots of waiting, the trade deadline heater is starting to thaw out. Hopefully, there are plenty more deals like this over the next 36-plus hours. Make sure to keep your eyes peeled here as we get closer to it.
